scope: Focused primary-source rereading for the new PD request-level SLO routing and tail-latency proposal. No new papers were added, no framework implementation or PD/GPU experiment was performed, and no novelty or performance claim is established by this record. Publication identities and additional mechanism evidence remain in the earlier immutable audits referenced below.

papers.title: Splitwise: Efficient Generative LLM Inference Using Phase Splitting
papers.finding: The cluster scheduler simultaneously assigns prompt and token machines using pending-token JSQ; simultaneous assignment supports layerwise transfer overlap. Serialized and layerwise transfer have different prompt-size and interference conditions.

papers.title: Mooncake: A KVCache-centric Disaggregated Architecture for LLM Serving
papers.finding: Prefill placement considers prefix reuse, queueing, execution and transfer estimates. Algorithm 1 returns both prefill and decoding instances and includes TTFT/TBT-based rejection; these mechanisms are baselines rather than new contributions of the proposal.

papers.title: Arrow: Adaptive Scheduling Mechanisms for Disaggregated LLM Inference Architecture
papers.version_note: Author arXiv v2; unresolved independent publication identity in the existing survey.
papers.finding: The global scheduler selects a prefill instance and then selects another instance after prefill completion, with the latter pulling KV. Its SLO-aware global scheduling uses real-time request and instance state. Post-prefill decode selection is therefore a direct existing baseline.

papers.title: Libra
papers.finding: Libra combines global request splitting/routing with local SLO-aware batching and chunk KV transfer. Its least-loaded micro-request placement belongs to a broader action space than fixed-role prompt-boundary PD routing.

papers.title: TaiChi
papers.version_note: Future SC 2026 program identity; this anchor uses the local author arXiv v1 only.
papers.finding: The latency-shifting discussion explicitly describes reallocating latency across phases and requests. It motivates separating reduced avoidable waiting from transferring delay to other requests.

papers.title: FluidPD
papers.version_note: Author arXiv v1; unresolved independent publication identity in the existing survey.
papers.finding: Decode pressure includes active and reserved KV, current batch and the largest SLO-compatible decode batch. This directly supports distinguishing active, reserved and allocable decode capacity in routing.

papers.title: Beyond Prediction: Tail-Aware Scheduling for LLM Inference
papers.finding: The paper documents forced preemption, batch-dependent service rate and mixed distributions as challenges to the basic queueing assumptions. Its appendix distinguishes global instance dispatch from UniBoost's within-instance scheduling and evaluates composition with random, round-robin and JSQ dispatch.

papers.title: Llumnix
papers.finding: Live migration pipelines append-only KV copying with ongoing decode and then copies the remaining suffix. It is an alternative to the proposal's deliberately excluded post-commit rebinding or active decode migration.

workload_provenance.mooncake: Arrival, length and remapped block-hash fields were previously verified in evidence/web-verification.json. Reconstructed prompts must not be described as original production text.

agentx.scope: Optional multi-turn long-context workload for the new proposal. Fixed source identifiers and downloaded artifact hashes were recorded by the existing local parameterized-scheduler project; this research repository did not redownload the large trace.

interpretation_limits: The cited papers establish direct prior art for early joint P/D selection, cache/SLO-aware routing and post-prefill D selection. The proposed provisional lifecycle, avoidable-tail headroom and any end-to-end improvement remain unimplemented hypotheses. Historical framework audits do not establish current upstream support for the proposed protocol.
